design.affected_system: non-clinical emergency call handling, unit readiness, and incident support network
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for emergency response readiness and coverage schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule emergency response readiness and coverage schedule
pair demand-, skill-, rest-, maintenance-, and coverage-constrained scheduling with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Calls, incidents, dispositions, unit states, travel, scene time, and outcomes remain distinct.
Any operational recommendation requires agency safety review and cannot automate high-stakes dispatch.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for emergency response readiness and coverage schedule.

constraints.description: The emergency response readiness and allocation schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: emergency communications director and public-safety operations chief
design.decision_question: When should shifts, standby posts, maintenance, training, and mutual-aid coverage operate?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The emergency response readiness and allocation schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.decision_object: emergency response readiness and coverage schedule
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for emergency response readiness and coverage schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: demand-, skill-, rest-, maintenance-, and coverage-constrained scheduling
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority demand-hours below minimum deployable coverage

design.intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting emergency response readiness and coverage schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority demand-hours below minimum deployable coverage
distributional gap in priority demand-hours below minimum deployable coverage
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a proposed readiness roster staffed, safe, negotiated, or operated.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for emergency response readiness and coverage schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

design.title: Schedule emergency readiness and coverage
transportability_risks: Call coding, dispatch policy, mutual aid, geography, traffic, staffing, and incident mix differ.
Recorded response time may omit call processing, staging, or outcome quality.

family.affected_system: non-clinical emergency call handling, unit readiness, and incident support network
claim_boundary: Service requests measure reported workload, not verified incidents, need, harm, or resolution.
Assignments and schedules are proposed operations, not completed work or public outcomes.
Design records do not establish agency adoption, deployment, productivity, or resident impact.
family.decision_owner: emergency communications director and public-safety operations chief
family.description: Eight decisions for response-gap diagnosis, demand forecasting, readiness portfolios, station siting, unit allocation, coverage schedules, surge stress, and system evaluation.
family.title: Emergency response readiness and allocation

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
